candidate.title: ICE
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina ICE (inosine chemical erasing) component schematic: untreated-control and acrylonitrile-treated RNA followed by separate RT/PCR blocks, yielding control cDNA versus a blocked modified fragment. Both arms belong to one assay. Downstream NGS is described by the card and explains the readout but is not drawn as another operation. The matching collection page is secondary evidence; its extra chemistry panel, application and library-kit lists do not expand the assigned PNG. The primary 2010 abstract supports ICE cyanoethylation plus reverse transcription, not a complete NGS library implementation.

operations.label: Reverse transcription / PCR amplification
operations.description: Attempt the separately depicted RT/PCR block on cyanoethylated RNA. Modified inosine blocks read-through and production of the corresponding amplifiable cDNA, shown by the red X.
operations.mechanism: Reverse transcription is inhibited by the modified inosine. The diagram combines RT and PCR and does not show a separate physical stop product.
operations.information_effect: The treated fragment's negative contribution relative to untreated cDNA supplies the chemical contrast for identifying RNA inosine. In the card's downstream sequencing context, this contrast supports A-to-I editing assignments; G-coded control sequence alone does not distinguish inosine from an ordinary guanosine. This is an interpretation of the two depicted outcomes, not a drawn analysis step. It does not imply that all treated RNAs fail or every missing read is an editing event. Catalogue limitations include nonlinear PCR bias and polymerase errors.
